To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
soil salinity induced cross tolerance to subsequent drought stress in tomatoes is associated with the enhancement of cyclic electron flow and proton motive force.

soil salinity induced cross tolerance to subsequent drought stress in tomatoes through the enhancement of non photochemical quencher (NPQ), cyclic electron flow (CEF) and proton motive force (PMF) that trade off between photoprotections and photochemistry reactions.

soil salinity pretreatments induced non-photochemical quenching of chlorophyll (Chl) fluorescence and cyclic electron (CEF), thus enhancing photosystem I (PSI) activity, proton motive force (PMF), and thylakoid ATP synthase (ATPase) activity in tomato leaves, thereby alleviating the damage caused by subsequent drought.

the photosynthetic response mechanism of soil salinization induced cross tolerance to subsequent drought stress in the tomato leaves.
the photosynthetic responses in tomato plants under soil salinity and subsequent drought stress.
the photosynthetic responses of tomato plants to soil salinity and subsequent drought stress.

salinity pretreatment can enhance drought resistance in plants, and the mechanism may be associated with the enhancement of non-photochemical quenching and cyclic electron flow.
soil salinity induced tolerance to the subsequent drought is a complex process that involves multiple physiological and biochemical changes.

soil salinity pretreatments could enhance drought resistance of tomato plants through inducing NPQ, enhancing CEF and maintaining pmf that trade-off between photoprotections and photochemistry reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

soil salinity pretreated tomato plants had the capacity to enhance the photosynthesis efficiency and maintain the thylakoids structure integrity in the subsequent drought stress, and this was attributed to the enhanced NPQ, CEF, and pmf in the chloroplasts.

the cross tolerance of tomato leaves to drought stress after NaCl treatment is mainly attributed to the enhancement of NPQ and pmf, which could alleviate the damage of thylakoid membranes and ATP synthase caused by the subsequent drought stress.
salt stress pretreatment induced a series of photosynthetic acclimate, including enhanced NPQ, maintained CEF and pmF, thus alleviated the damage of drought stress in photosynthetic apparatus.

soil salinization could induce cross tolerance in tomato plants to subsequent drought stress through photosynthetic acclamation.

the soil salinity treatment can enhance drought tolerance in tomato plants by enhancing the photosynthetic capacity of the plant to cope with drought stress, thus providing a theoretical basis for the application of soil salinity treatment in the cultivation of tomato plants.
